question: How should E composition be implemented in layers with explicit reduction contracts, avoiding monolithic integration failure?
purpose: Architectural decomposition only; no additional scientific theory beyond E0

implementation_ladder.display: E1 hierarchy/runtime -> E2 delayed coupling -> E3 RBS composition -> E4 observation chain -> E5 integrated perturbation

ordered_checkpoints.label: hierarchy/runtime
ordered_checkpoints.adds: minimal two-area laminar hierarchy, heterogeneous populations/parameters, FF/FB ownership, zero delay

ordered_checkpoints.label: delayed coupling
ordered_checkpoints.adds: validated delay machinery G -> tau_ij -> X with delay_state continuation

ordered_checkpoints.label: RBS composition
ordered_checkpoints.adds: validated RBS/RBD slice on selected populations under dot W = 0

ordered_checkpoints.label: observation chain
ordered_checkpoints.adds: X,H -> Q -> Phi -> P -> Y using Experiment-A semantics

integration_monotonicity_principle.statement: Adding a validated TFNE layer must not invalidate the previously established semantics of lower layers
integration_monotonicity_principle.containment: E1 subset E2 subset E3 subset E4

reduction_contracts.when: E4 observation operators removed or bypassed

terminology.heterogeneous_populations: distinct population labels, layer/cell-type routing, and parameter sets within one emitter family
terminology.heterogeneous_emitter_equations: genuinely different F_X realizations across populations
terminology.rule: Do not describe E1 heterogeneous populations/parameters as heterogeneous emitter equations unless F_X families actually differ

methodological_inheritance_from_D3.E5_phenotype_rule: phenotype evidence = perturbation effect minus mechanism-null effect
methodological_inheritance_from_D3.example: FF/FB spectral claim requires contribution beyond matched null/ablation, not Y_FF != Y_baseline alone
